'''Brian David Ripley''' [[FRSE]] (born 29 April 1952) is a British [[statistician]]. From 1990, he was professor of [[applied statistics]] at the [[University of Oxford]] and also a [[professorial fellow]] at [[St Peter's College, Oxford|St Peter's College]]. He retired August 2014 due to ill health.<ref>[https://www.stats.ox.ac.uk/~ripley/ Professor Ripley's Homepage at Oxford University]. Accessed 8 June 2024.</ref>

==Biography==
Ripley has made contributions to the fields of [[spatial statistics]] and [[pattern recognition]]. His work on [[artificial neural network]]s in the 1990s helped to bring aspects of [[machine learning]] and [[data mining]] to the attention of statistical audiences.<ref>For instance, his book ''Pattern Recognition and Neural Networks'' was reviewed in the ''[[Journal of the American Statistical Association]]'': {{citation|title=Reviewed Works: ''Neural Networks for Pattern Recognition'' by C. M. Bishop; ''Pattern Recognition and Neural Networks'' by B. D. Ripley|first=Nicholas|last=Lange|journal=[[Journal of the American Statistical Association]]|volume=92|issue=440|date=December 1997|pages=1642–1645|jstor=2965437|doi=10.2307/2965437}}.</ref> He emphasised the value of [[robust statistics]] in his books ''Pattern Recognition and Neural Networks'' and ''Modern Applied Statistics with S''.

Ripley helped develop the [[S-PLUS]] programming language<ref name="SProg">{{cite book |last1=Venables |first1=W.N. |last2=Ripley |first2=B.D. |title=S programming |date=2000 |publisher=Springer |isbn=0-387-98966-8 |url=https://www.stats.ox.ac.uk/pub/MASS3/Sprog/ |access-date=8 June 2024}}</ref><ref name="MASS">{{cite book |last1=Venables |first1=W.N. |last2=Ripley |first2=B.D. |title=Modern applied statistics with S |date=2002 |publisher=Springer |isbn=0-387-95457-0 |edition=4th |url=https://www.stats.ox.ac.uk/pub/MASS4/ |access-date=8 June 2024}}</ref> and its [[open source]] derivative [[R (programming language)|R]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.r-project.org/contributors.html |title=Contributors |publisher=The [[R Foundation for Statistical Computing]] |date=April 2024 |access-date=9 June 2024 }}</ref> He co-authored two books based on S, ''S Programming'' and ''Modern Applied Statistics with S''.<ref name="SProg" /><ref name="MASS" /> Since mid-1997 he is a member of the "R Core Team"<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cran.r-project.org/doc/FAQ/R-FAQ.html#What-is-CRAN_003f |title=R FAQ: What is R?|author=Kurt Hornik and the R Core Team |publisher=[[R_package#Comprehensive_R_Archive_Network_(CRAN)|CRAN]] |date=2023 |access-date=9 June 2024 }}</ref> and from 2000 to 2021 he was one of the most active committers to the R core.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Eddelbuettel|first=Dirk|date=2021-03-20|title=An Ode to Stable Interfaces: R and R Core Deserve So Much Praise|url=http://dirk.eddelbuettel.com/blog/2021/03/20/#ode_to_r_stability|url-status=live|access-date=8 June 2024|website=Thinking Inside the Box|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210321042730/https://dirk.eddelbuettel.com/blog/2021/03/20/ |archive-date=21 March 2021 }}</ref> The [[R package|package]] MASS<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cran.r-project.org/package=MASS |title=MASS: Support Functions and Datasets for Venables and Ripley's MASS |last=Ripley |first=Brian |authorlink=Brian D. Ripley |last2=Venables |first2=Bill |last3=Bates |first3= Douglas M. |last4=Hornik |first4=Kurt |last5=Gebhardt |first5=Albrecht |last6=Firth |first6=David |publisher=[[R_package#Comprehensive_R_Archive_Network_(CRAN)|CRAN]] |date=26 April 2024 |accessdate=8 June 2024 }}</ref> is one of only fifteen "recommended packages"<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cran.r-project.org/doc/FAQ/R-FAQ.html#Add_002don-packages-from-CRAN |title=R FAQ: Add-on packages from CRAN |author=Kurt Hornik and the R Core Team |publisher=[[R_package#Comprehensive_R_Archive_Network_(CRAN)|CRAN]] |date=2023 |access-date=8 June 2024 }}</ref> for R (with June 2024 more than 20,900<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ |title=CRAN: Contributed Packages |access-date=9 June 2024 }}</ref>).

He was educated at the [[University of Cambridge]], where he was awarded both the [[Smith's Prize]] (at the time awarded to the best graduate essay writer who had been undergraduate at Cambridge in that cohort) and the [[Rollo Davidson Prize]]. The university also awarded him the [[Adams Prize]] in 1987 for an essay entitled ''Statistical Inference for Spatial Processes'', later published as a book.<ref>{{cite book|last=Ripley|first=B. D.|title=Statistical Inference for Spatial Processes|year=1988|publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]|isbn=0-521-35234-7|pages=iv, vii}}</ref> He served on the faculty of [[Imperial College, London]] from 1976 until 1983, at which point he moved to the [[University of Strathclyde]].<ref name="profile">[https://www.stats.ox.ac.uk/~ripley/profile.html Profile of Professor Brian D Ripley] (Last edited 1 October 1999 by Brian Ripley). Accessed 8 June 2024.</ref> 

In 2026, he was awarded the [[Rousseeuw Prize for Statistics]] alongside four other contributors to R. He told the BBC he would spend "some, maybe all" of his $200k share of the prize on improving R.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Gudge |first1=Ethan |title=Prof Brian Ripley on developing R to manage the world's data |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c1wydlwen7eo |access-date=22 June 2026 |work=BBC News |date=21 June 2026}}</ref>

==Authored books==
* Ripley, B. D. (1981) ''Spatial Statistics''. Wiley, 252pp. {{ISBN|0-471-08367-4}}.
* Ripley, B. D. (1983) ''Stochastic Simulation''. Wiley, {{ISBN|0-471-81884-4}}.
* {{cite book|last=Ripley|first=B. D.|title=Statistical Inference for Spatial Processes|year=1988|publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]|isbn=0-521-35234-7}}
* Ripley, B. D. (1996) ''Pattern Recognition and Neural Networks''. Cambridge University Press. 403 pages. {{ISBN|0-521-46086-7}}.
* Venables, W. N. and Ripley, B. D. (2000) ''S Programming''. Springer, 264pp. {{ISBN|978-0-387-98966-2}}.
* Venables, W. N. and Ripley, B. D. (2002) ''Modern Applied Statistics with S'' (Fourth Edition; previous editions published as ''Modern Applied Statistics with S-PLUS'' in 1994, 1997 & 1999). Springer, 462pp. {{ISBN|978-0-387-95457-8}}.
